highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.151.0 restores faster CPU image rendering and reduces overhead in color and text hot paths.
highlights_body: The Skia m151 release also adds span-based parsing and .NET 11 WebAssembly archives. Existing .NET 8-10 WebAssembly toolchain mappings are retained.

breaking.title: Remove whitespace immediately after the color prefix
breaking.body: SKColor.Parse and TryParse now reject whitespace directly after # in six- and eight-digit forms, matching the stricter short forms. Remove that internal whitespace before parsing; surrounding whitespace and case-insensitive hexadecimal input remain supported.

bullets.detail: Updates the bundled renderer from m150 to m151 without changing the C API in the milestone sync.

bullets.lead: Parse colors and four-byte tags from spans
bullets.detail: Adds ReadOnlySpan<char> parsing for SKColor and SKFourByteTag, allowing slices of larger buffers without allocating substrings. The tag parser preserves padding, truncation, and low-byte packing semantics.

bullets.lead: CPU scaled and tiled images regain their fast path
bullets.detail: Restores the legacy shader-context raster path for scaled or tiled bitmap draws, addressing high CPU usage and frame drops.
Fixes corrupt GPU text teardown, stencil-clear coordinate tracking and preservation, and dirty-state recovery when a resolve task fails to execute.
Single-value SKColor-to-SKColorF and SKPMColor conversions avoid native round trips while preserving exact results.

bullets.lead: Less temporary storage for shaped text
bullets.detail: SKShaper reads glyph results through spans rather than intermediate array copies, while HarfBuzzSharp.Buffer.AddUtf8(string) pools its encoding storage instead of allocating an array per call.
SKImage.FromEncodedData(SKData, SKRectI) deterministically disposes the full decoded image when Subset returns a different instance, while preserving same-instance returns.
Adds Emscripten 5.0.6 native libraries and the new exception-handling instructions required by .NET 11 preview 6 and later in this release. .NET 8 continues to use 3.1.34 and .NET 9/10 use 3.1.56.

contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: Added .NET 11 WebAssembly native archives, introduced cross-backend visual regression coverage, and removed redundant WASM build defines

preview_summaries.v4.151.0-preview.1.1: Preview 1 opened the line with the Skia m151 engine update.
preview_summaries.v4.151.0-preview.2.1: Preview 2 added span-based color and tag parsing, reduced shaping allocations, and fixed corrupt GPU text teardown. Color parsing no longer accepts whitespace directly after #.
preview_summaries.v4.151.0-rc.1.1: Release Candidate 1 restored the faster CPU bitmap shader path, added matching .NET 11 WebAssembly archives and exception handling, and fixed subset-image resource retention.

harfbuzz_summary: Buffer.AddUtf8(string) uses pooled encoding storage instead of allocating an array per call. Tag.Parse adds a span overload and removes its scratch array while preserving existing packing semantics.

v4.151.0-preview.1.1.headline: Preview 1 opened the Skia m151 line without changing the managed API surface.

v4.151.0-preview.2.1.headline: Preview 2 added span-based color and tag parsing, reduced shaping allocations, and corrected malformed native text cleanup.

v4.151.0-rc.1.1.headline: The release candidate restored CPU bitmap performance, optimized color math, fixed subset-image cleanup, and aligned .NET 11 WebAssembly assets and exception handling.

v4.151.0.headline: SkiaSharp 4.151.0 promotes the release candidate to stable without additional collected changes.
